card_summary: A study by TV Technology found that repurposing traditional TV ads for Connected TV (CTV) is a missed opportunity. The study was conducted to analyze ad effectiveness. The study's findings have implications for live signal transport, particularly in terms of latency and signal integrity. Broadcasters using ST 2110, NDI, or SRT for real-time transport must ensure frame-accuracy and low latency to maintain signal quality, especially when inserting ads into live CTV streams over 12G-SDI or compressed with JPEG XS.

Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Transport Latency by 30%

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their IP-cores for real-time video transport over 12G-SDI. This development is significant as it enables broadcast engineers to reduce latency and increase signal integrity in live production environments. The technology is particularly relevant for applications where ultra-low latency and high-quality video are essential, such as live sports and news broadcasts.

Operational ROI

The introduction of JPEG XS compression into 12G-SDI transport systems can significantly reduce transmission costs and latency. By compressing video signals in real-time, broadcasters can achieve a 30% reduction in latency compared to traditional uncompressed transport methods. This reduction in latency can be particularly beneficial in live production environments where every millisecond counts. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression can simplify signal routing and reduce the required hardware rack footprint, resulting in lower operational costs and increased efficiency.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as using multiple 3G-SDI links to transport 4K video, the use of JPEG XS compression over 12G-SDI offers a more efficient and cost-effective solution. The reduced latency and increased signal integrity provided by JPEG XS compression can also enable new applications, such as remote production and virtual studios, which require ultra-low latency and high-quality video. Furthermore, the use of JPEG XS compression can reduce the complexity of signal routing and distribution, resulting in lower maintenance and support costs.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into 12G-SDI transport systems is designed to be compliant with relevant broadcast standards, including SMPTE ST 2110 and NMOS. The use of JPEG XS compression also supports the use of AES67 audio over IP, enabling the transport of high-quality audio signals over the same network as the video signals. In terms of cybersecurity, the use of JPEG XS compression does not introduce any new security risks, as it is a compression algorithm that operates on the video signal itself, rather than relying on external software or dependencies. The compression algorithm is also designed to be compatible with existing broadcast equipment and infrastructure, including Genlock and 12G-SDI interfaces.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy JPEG XS compression over 12G-SDI, broadcast engineers will require a compatible IP-core, such as the intoPIX IP-core, and a 12G-SDI interface. The system will also require a sufficient network bandwidth to support the compressed video signals, which can be achieved using a 10GbE or 25GbE network infrastructure.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression algorithm is designed to be compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast equipment and infrastructure. The algorithm is also compatible with SRT and RIST protocols, enabling secure and reliable transport of compressed video signals over IP networks.
  • What to Watch: Broadcast engineers should track the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which are expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression and other emerging technologies. Additionally, the development of new IP-cores and interfaces that support JPEG XS compression will be important to watch, as they will enable further innovation and adoption of this technology in live production environments.

The introduction of JPEG XS compression into 12G-SDI transport systems signals a significant shift towards more efficient and cost-effective live production workflows. As this technology continues to evolve, broadcast engineers should prioritize the development of compatible infrastructure and equipment to support the adoption of JPEG XS compression in their workflows.

Analysis: ST 2110 and NMOS protocols can facilitate efficient ad insertion in CTV workflows, but repurposed traditional TV ads may not fully leverage these standards, potentially limiting bitrate and latency optimization.
